spot.name: Tianning Temple
spot.bio: Buddhist temple beside the Grand Canal with the 13-storey, 153.79 m Tianning Pagoda, finished in 2007.

spot.name: China Dinosaur Park
spot.bio: Theme park with rides, dancing dinosaurs and a museum of fossils including a Sinosauropteryx skeleton.

spot.name: Hongmei Park
spot.bio: Large lakeside park with the Writing Pagoda, Red Plum Pavilion and a flamingo pond.

spot.name: Dongpo Park
spot.bio: Small Grand Canal island park with a Su Dongpo academy hall and statue and Qianlong palace foundations.

spot.name: Canal 5 Creative Campus
spot.bio: Former textile mill on the Grand Canal turned into art studios, restaurants and museums.

spot.name: Changzhou Museum
spot.bio: Museum of over 20,000 relics, from Spring and Autumn green porcelain to Ming and Qing paintings.

spot.name: Yancheng Safari Park
spot.bio: Wild animal park with walk-through areas and a drive-through route where visitors can bring their own vehicle.

spot.name: Zhou Enlai's Former Residence
spot.bio: Childhood home of Zhou Enlai, who was born here in 1898 and lived here for his first twelve years.

spot.name: Zhou Enlai Memorial Hall
spot.bio: Exhibitions on the life and work of Zhou Enlai, set in his home city of Huai'an.

spot.name: Wu Cheng'en's Former Residence
spot.bio: Home of Ming-dynasty writer Wu Cheng'en, author of Journey to the West, in Datong Lane in Hexia.

spot.name: China Water Transport Museum
spot.bio: Museum on Huai'an's role in shipping grain along the Grand Canal to the imperial capital.

spot.name: Huai'an Government House
spot.bio: One of very few surviving prefectural yamen in China, first built in 1370 and restored after fires.

spot.name: Iris Chang Memorial Hall
spot.bio: Memorial to Iris Chang, author of The Rape of Nanking, with exhibitions on her life and the Nanjing Massacre.

spot.name: Huai'an Museum
spot.bio: City museum on the history and culture of Huai'an, in Qingjiangpu District.

placements.name: Journey to the West Amusement Park

spot.name: Journey to the West Amusement Park
spot.bio: Theme park built around the characters and stories of Wu Cheng'en's novel Journey to the West.

spot.name: Huai'an Zoo
spot.bio: City zoo founded in 1958 and moved to its present site in 2012, with imported and native animals.

spot.name: Zhou Enlai's Childhood School
spot.bio: Family school where Zhou Enlai studied as a child with his brother and two sisters.

spot.name: Tongli
spot.bio: Canal town in Wujiang, home of the only UNESCO-listed Suzhou garden outside downtown.

spot.name: Luzhi
spot.bio: Historic canal town in Wuzhong District, 18 km east of Suzhou, home to Baosheng Temple.

spot.name: Shen's Residence
spot.bio: Hall built in 1742 by descendants of Shen Wansan, southeast of Fu'an Bridge in Zhouzhuang.

spot.name: Retreat and Reflection Garden
spot.bio: Classical garden in Tongli, UNESCO-listed in 2001 and the only one of its kind outside downtown Suzhou.

spot.name: Mount Huaguo
spot.bio: Mountain said to inspire the Monkey King's home in Journey to the West, topped by Jiangsu's highest peak.

spot.name: Lian Island
spot.bio: Jiangsu's largest island, 9 km long and 80% forested, linked to the mainland by a long sea dyke.

spot.name: Yuntai Mountain
spot.bio: Coastal range of waterfalls and peaks in Lianyungang that includes Mount Huaguo.

spot.name: Yuwan Scenic Area
spot.bio: Scenic area of waterfalls, rocks and cliffs at the foot of Yuntai Mountain.

spot.name: Qinshan Island
spot.bio: Sea island off Ganyu, one of 26 small islands along Jiangsu's coast and a national 4A attraction.

spot.name: Lianyungang Museum
spot.bio: The city's main museum, on Chaoyang Road East in Haizhou District, with local history exhibits.

spot.name: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum
spot.bio: Memorial tomb of Sun Yat-sen at the foot of Purple Mountain's second peak, built between 1926 and 1929.

spot.name: Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum
spot.bio: Mausoleum of the Hongwu Emperor, founder of the Ming, with a mile-long sacred way lined with stone camels and elephants.

spot.name: Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall
spot.wiki: Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders
spot.bio: Memorial to the 1937 Nanjing Massacre with two partly excavated burial sites, sculptures and a museum.

spot.name: Presidential Palace
spot.bio: Seat of the Republic of China presidency from 1927 to 1949, now the China Modern History Museum.

spot.name: Nanjing Museum
spot.bio: Provincial museum of Jiangsu, one of China's first, with eleven halls of bronzes, silk and a door from the Ming porcelain tower.

spot.name: Purple Mountain
spot.bio: Nanjing's highest hill at 448.9 m, home to the tombs of Sun Yat-sen, the Hongwu Emperor and Sun Quan.

spot.name: Xuanwu Lake
spot.bio: City lake of about 444 hectares with five islets joined by arch bridges, beside the Ming wall, with paddle boats.

spot.name: Zhonghua Gate
spot.bio: Southern gate of the Ming city wall, among the best-preserved gate complexes in the world, with courtyards and an archery range.

placements.name: Ruins of the Ming Dynasty Imperial Palace

spot.name: Ruins of the Ming Dynasty Imperial Palace
spot.bio: Remains of the early Ming palace, called the Forbidden City of Nanjing, with Meridian Gate arches and carved stone bridges.

spot.name: Qinhuai River
spot.bio: 110 km tributary of the Yangtze through the city, with a scenic belt of old-town sights, snack stalls and canal boats.

spot.name: Meihuashan
spot.bio: Plum Blossom Hill on Purple Mountain, planted with about 35,000 plum trees of more than 360 varieties.

spot.name: Great Bao'en Temple Ruins Park
spot.bio: Ruins park on the site of the Great Bao'en Temple, with a museum and a rebuilt Porcelain Tower with city views.

spot.name: Jiming Temple
spot.bio: Buddhist temple near Xuanwu Lake, one of the oldest in Nanjing and called its most popular temple.

spot.name: Drum Tower
spot.bio: Ming-era drum tower, rebuilt in the Qing, at the centre of a small park on a roundabout at Gulou station.

spot.name: Qixia Temple
spot.bio: Buddhist temple on Qixia Mountain whose Thousand Buddha Rock holds 297 niches and 515 statues, 22 km from downtown.

spot.name: Yuhuatai Scenic Area
spot.bio: Memorial park south of the old city, best known for the Yuhuatai Martyrs' Cemetery.

spot.name: Meiling Palace
spot.bio: Villa built in 1934 for Soong Mei-ling on Purple Mountain, restored, with a bookshop and cafe upstairs.

spot.name: Hongshan Forest Zoo
spot.bio: Zoo in Xuanwu District covering 68 hectares across the Xiao Hongshan, Da Hongshan and Fangniu Mountain areas.

spot.name: Jiangsu Art Museum
spot.bio: Jiangsu's provincial art museum, which has a new branch and an old branch.

spot.name: Nanjing Municipal Museum
spot.bio: City museum inside Chaotian Palace, founded in 1978, with entry included in the palace ticket.

spot.name: Gan Family Compound
spot.bio: Qing-era merchant courtyard house on Zhongshan South Road in the old town, now open to visitors.

spot.name: John Rabe's Former Residence
spot.bio: Former home of John Rabe, now a museum on his life and the Nanjing International Safety Zone.

placements.name: Yangtze River Crossing Campaign Victory Memorial Hall

spot.name: Yangtze River Crossing Campaign Victory Memorial Hall
spot.bio: Museum on the 1949 Communist crossing of the Yangtze and the capture of Nanjing, on Dujiang Road.

spot.name: Liji Alley Comfort Station Site
spot.bio: Former wartime comfort station, one of the largest in Asia, now a museum entered by appointment.

spot.name: Nanjing Yuejiang Lou
spot.bio: Tower on Lion Hill overlooking the Yangtze, called one of the best viewpoints in the city.

spot.name: Nanjing Underwater World
spot.bio: Aquarium on the south side of Purple Mountain, near the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum.

spot.name: Nanjing Science and Technology Museum
spot.bio: Science and technology museum on Zixinghua Road in Yuhuatai District, with free admission.

spot.name: Sifang Contemporary Art Museum
spot.bio: Contemporary art museum in Pukou designed by Steven Holl, opened in 2013, with an art lake.

spot.name: Pearl Spring Scenic Area
spot.bio: Resort area in Pukou with a walkable Great Wall replica, a wildlife park and a cable car.

placements.name: Haohe River Scenic and Historic Spot

spot.name: Haohe River Scenic and Historic Spot
spot.bio: A moat-like river ring around Nantong's old city, with evening boat trips and several museums along its banks.

spot.name: Nantong Museum
spot.bio: One of China's oldest museums, founded in 1905 by Zhang Jian beside the Haohe, covering Nantong's history.

spot.name: Nantong Forest Safari Park
spot.bio: Wildlife park opened in 2018 with nearly 20,000 animals of over 300 species, including pandas and kangaroos.

spot.name: Wenfeng Park
spot.bio: Old city park beside Wenfeng Tower, a 39 m five-storey tower dating from 1620.

placements.name: Nantong Sendi Ice and Snow Park

spot.name: Nantong Sendi Ice and Snow Park
spot.bio: Indoor ice and snow park next to the Forest Safari Park, with tickets from RMB 158.

spot.name: Five Mountains
spot.bio: Group of Yangtze hills including Langshan, Junshan and Jianshan, with a riverside greenway and river views.

spot.name: Humble Administrator's Garden
spot.bio: Suzhou's largest classical garden at 78 mu, a UNESCO World Heritage component in the old city's northeast.

spot.name: Tiger Hill
spot.bio: Hill park said to resemble a crouching tiger, topped by a 48 m leaning seven-storey brick pagoda.

spot.name: Lingering Garden
spot.bio: One of the largest classical gardens in Suzhou, part of the UNESCO-listed Classical Gardens of Suzhou.

spot.name: Master of the Nets Garden
spot.bio: Small classical garden founded in 1140 and rebuilt in 1770, UNESCO-listed and among Suzhou's best proportioned.

spot.name: Lion Grove Garden
spot.bio: UNESCO-listed classical garden known for its rockery maze, close to the Humble Administrator's Garden.

spot.name: Canglang Pavilion
spot.bio: One of Suzhou's oldest scholar gardens, UNESCO-listed and more densely wooded than the others.

spot.name: Suzhou Museum
spot.bio: I.M. Pei's museum beside the Humble Administrator's Garden, with a recreated Ming scholar's study.

spot.name: Pingjiang Road
spot.bio: Historic street in the northeast old town, paved with hand-cut stones and lined with traditional-style shops.

spot.name: Shantang Street
spot.bio: Restored canal street about 3.8 km long, linking Changmen to Tiger Hill, with shops in traditional style.

spot.name: Mudu
spot.bio: Water town in Wuzhong District, famed for its history and visited six times by the Qianlong Emperor.

spot.name: Couple's Retreat Garden
spot.bio: Early 20th-century UNESCO-listed garden whose many small rooms and covered walkways suit a rainy day.

spot.name: Mountain Villa with Embracing Beauty
spot.bio: Rock and water garden at 272 Jingde Road inside the Embroidery Museum, UNESCO-listed in 1997.

spot.name: Garden of Cultivation
spot.bio: One of Suzhou's best-preserved Ming gardens, UNESCO-listed, with the best part at the back.

spot.name: North Temple Pagoda
spot.bio: Nine-storey, 76 m pagoda at Bao'en Temple, once eleven storeys, visible from the train station.

spot.name: Temple of Mystery
spot.bio: Taoist temple at the centre of old Suzhou, founded in the 3rd century, with small shops around the hall.

spot.name: Pan Gate
spot.bio: Combined water and land gate in the old city wall's southwest corner, rebuilt in the 14th century.

spot.name: Jinji Lake
spot.bio: Freshwater lake of 7.18 km2 in the middle of Suzhou Industrial Park, with two man-made islands.

spot.name: Ligongdi
spot.bio: A 1,400 m causeway across Jinji Lake, built in the Guangxu reign (1874-1908).

spot.name: Suzhou Ferris Wheel
spot.bio: Ferris wheel on the east bank of Jinji Lake, rebuilt in 2025 at 128 m, with views over the lake.

spot.name: Guanqian Street
spot.bio: Pedestrian-only shopping street near the centre, with craft shops and local restaurants in its back streets.

spot.name: Twin Pagodas
spot.bio: Pair of Northern Song brick pagodas beside the remains of an Arhat temple, with carved stone pillars.

spot.name: Suzhou Confucian Temple
spot.bio: Song-dynasty Confucian temple founded in 1035 that holds the Stele Inscription Museum and four great Song steles.

spot.name: Xiyuan Temple
spot.bio: Buddhist temple just west of Lingering Garden in Wuzhong District.

spot.name: Suzhou Opera Museum
spot.wiki: Suzhou Museum of Opera and Theatre
spot.bio: Theatre museum in a Ming latticed-wood theatre, with Kunqu instruments, scripts, masks and costumes.

spot.name: Suzhou Pingtan Museum
spot.bio: Museum of Pingtan, storytelling and ballad singing in the Suzhou dialect, with live performances.

spot.name: City God Temple of Suzhou
spot.bio: Chinese folk temple dedicated to the City God among the old streets of central Suzhou, free to enter.

spot.name: Suzhou Archaeological Museum
spot.bio: One of Suzhou's newest museums, showing artefacts from archaeological sites in the Suzhou area.

spot.name: Grand Buddha at Ling Shan
spot.bio: A bronze Buddha statue over 80 m tall at Lingshan on Lake Tai's north shore, one of the largest in China.

spot.name: Turtle Head Island
spot.bio: A peninsula on Lake Tai's northwest shore named for a turtle-shaped rock, known for cherry blossoms in March and April.

spot.name: Xihui Park
spot.bio: A state park west of Wuxi, set up in 1958, with Jichang Garden, the Second Spring under Heaven and a cable car up Mount Hui.

spot.name: Jichang Garden
spot.bio: A Ming-origin classical garden at the foot of Mount Hui that inspired gardens at the Summer Palace and Yuanming Yuan.

spot.name: Huishan Ancient Town
spot.bio: A historic district at the eastern foot of Huishan with traditional streets, old buildings and ancestral halls.

spot.name: Nianhua Bay
spot.bio: A Zen-themed town scenic area on the Lake Tai shore, just west of the Lingshan Scenic Area in Binhu District.

spot.name: Lihu Park
spot.bio: A free 300-acre park beside Lake Tai in Binhu District, with a Ferris wheel, a carousel and a maze.

spot.name: Liyuan Garden
spot.bio: A lakeside Chinese garden named for Fan Li, with a 100-year-old white wisteria nicknamed the Money Tree.

spot.name: Nanchang Street
spot.bio: A renovated canal street beside Qingming Bridge, the best-kept stretch of Wuxi's traditional canal town.

spot.name: Donglin Academy
spot.bio: A Northern Song academy founded in 1111, with Ming and Qing halls, a stone arch and a pool.

spot.name: Plum Garden
spot.bio: A Lake Tai botanical garden with about 4,000 fruit trees that blossom in spring, beside the old Rong family mansions.

spot.name: Wuxi Museum
spot.bio: A museum holding nearly 40,000 relics, from paintings and calligraphy to purple clay teapots and Huishan clay figurines.

spot.name: Dangkou Ancient Town
spot.bio: A 4A-rated ancient-town scenic area in Ehu town, Xishan District, free to enter.

spot.name: Jin Gui Park
spot.bio: A 48-hectare park in Binhu District, one of the city's largest, with cherry blossoms and tulips in March and April.

spot.name: Wuxi Zoo
spot.bio: A zoo and amusement park at the foot of Huishan with over 1,000 rare animals and giant panda research programmes.

spot.name: Wuxi Sunac Land
spot.bio: An amusement park in Binhu District with a 1,278 m roller coaster that reaches 118 km/h, reachable by Metro Line 1.

spot.name: Wuxi Sunac Sea World
spot.bio: A marine park in Binhu with sharks and rays, planned to hold about 1,500 marine species.

spot.name: Helu City Site
spot.bio: A museum on the site of King Helu of Wu's capital, housed in a phoenix-shaped building.

spot.name: Hongshan Archaeological Museum
spot.bio: A museum of the Hongshan archaeological site in Hongshan subdistrict, Xinwu District, free to enter.

spot.name: Lion Hill Han Tombs
spot.bio: Western Han tomb of a Chu king on Lion Hill, with a nearby museum of over 5,000 terracotta warriors.

spot.name: Xuzhou Museum
spot.bio: Museum founded in 1959 on a former Qianlong palace site, which also runs Xuzhou's Han tomb sites.

spot.name: Yunlong Lake
spot.bio: Large lake in southwest Xuzhou with Yunlong Mountain on its east side and the aquarium on Huxin Island.

spot.name: Yunlong Mountain
spot.bio: A 142 m hill of nine dragon-like peaks, with a Song-era crane pavilion; climb on foot or by cable car.

spot.name: Guishan Han Tombs
spot.bio: Rock-cut Western Han tomb of Liu Zhu, sixth king of Chu, with two corridors and five halls.

spot.name: Hubu Hill Ancient Architecture Complex
spot.bio: Ming and Qing courtyard houses of officials and merchants on Hubu Hill, two of them holding the Folk Museum.

spot.name: Huaihai Campaign Memorial Museum
spot.bio: Museum in a large park on the Huaihai Campaign, a major campaign of the Chinese Civil War.

spot.name: Quanshan National Forest Park
spot.bio: Forest park across the five peaks of Mount Quanshan, with arboretums and China's biggest bird garden.

spot.name: Slender West Lake
spot.bio: A narrow lake of pavilions, grown from Tang-era city moats and lined with Qing salt merchants' estates.

spot.name: Geyuan Garden
spot.bio: A Qing salt merchant's garden on Dongguan Street, known for its bamboo and stone, with sections for the four seasons.

spot.name: He Garden
spot.bio: The best-known private garden of the late Qing dynasty, with tea houses, open grottoes and pleasant views.

spot.name: Dongguan Street
spot.bio: An old-quarter street in eastern Yangzhou, lined with Geyuan Garden and the Taoist Wudangxing Palace.

spot.name: Daming Temple
spot.bio: A temple on Shugang Mountain tied to Jianzhen, who ordained monks here in 742 before going to Japan.

spot.name: Yangzhou Museum
spot.bio: Yangzhou's largest museum by Mingyue Lake, with a Grand Canal boat and a woodblock printing museum on site.

spot.name: China Grand Canal Museum
spot.bio: A modern museum on the Grand Canal heritage site in Sanwan wetland park.

spot.name: Xiaoqinhuai Canal
spot.bio: A canal through the old city centre, with the narrow lanes of a few surviving old blocks nearby.

spot.name: Wenchang Pavilion
spot.bio: The surviving pavilion of a Confucian academy, standing in the roundabout that marks Yangzhou's symbolic centre.

spot.name: Shi Kefa Memorial
spot.bio: Memorial temple for the Ming general Shi Kefa, who refused to surrender Yangzhou in 1645, with his clothing tomb.

spot.name: Tomb of Puhaddin
spot.bio: A park around the tomb of the Islamic missionary Puhaddin, with small exhibits on Yangzhou's Hui Muslim community.

spot.name: Yixing Ceramics Museum
spot.bio: One of China's earliest ceramics museums, with 107 relics from Neolithic pottery to Ming and Qing zisha teapots.

spot.name: Yixing Bamboo Sea
spot.bio: A national 4A bamboo forest park in Hufu town, 31 km southwest of Yixing city, among Wuxi's Eighteen Scenic Spots.

spot.name: Shanjuan Cave
spot.bio: A cave in Luoyan Mountain with upper, middle, lower and water caves and a boat ride on an underground river.

spot.name: Tuanjiu Scenic Area
spot.bio: A lake scenic area in Yixing rated 4A, with the Yiyuan garden and a plaza and park on its east shore.

spot.name: Longbeishan Forest Park
spot.bio: A 4A forest park on Renmin South Road in Yixing city, free to enter.

spot.name: Jinshan Temple
spot.bio: Buddhist temple climbing Jinshan Hill beside a lake, crowned by Cishou Pagoda and set in the White Snake legend.

spot.name: Jiaoshan
spot.bio: Yangtze island reached by boat, with Dinghui Temple and a stele forest of over 400 tablets.

spot.name: Beigu Hill
spot.bio: Steep hill on the Yangtze bank topped by Ganlu Temple, with views across to Jiaoshan and Jinshan.

spot.name: Zhenjiang Museum
spot.bio: Museum in the former British consulate buildings, with Wu bronzes, Six Dynasties celadon and Tang gold and silver.

spot.name: Nanshan Park
spot.bio: Forested hills south of the city with temples, springs and a hilltop pagoda looking over city and river.

spot.name: Zhulin Temple
spot.bio: Temple on Jia Hill hidden in a bamboo valley, reached by stone steps up five terraces of old trees.

spot.name: Tinglin Garden
spot.bio: Early 20th-century traditional-style garden named for the scholar Gu Yanwu, whose literary name was Tinglin.

spot.name: Bacheng Old Street
spot.bio: Stone-paved street of mainly late Qing Jiangnan-style buildings, about 280 m long.

spot.name: Shang Lake
spot.bio: Lake scenic area in Yushan Town, Changshu, with a bamboo boat ride through a crane reserve.

spot.name: Kunshan Opera Museum
spot.bio: Museum of Kunqu and other opera in Kunshan's Bacheng area, free to enter.

spot.name: Zheng He Park
spot.bio: Memorial park to Zheng He in Taicang, with a museum and a replica of a treasure ship.

spot.name: Yu Mountain
spot.bio: Hill 300 m high and 6.5 km long in northwest Changshu, with a Great Wall section and an old temple at the top.

spot.name: Shajiabang Scenic Area
spot.bio: Tourist village beside Yangcheng Lake in Changshu, with a scenic area called Shajiabang Resort.

spot.name: Lake Tai
spot.bio: The third largest freshwater lake in China, known for its fish and freshwater pearls and lined with scenic areas.

spot.name: Former Residence of Liu Brothers
spot.bio: The former home of linguist Liu Bannong and erhu composer Liu Tianhua, with six halls on the three Liu brothers.

spot.name: Xu Xiake's Former Residence
spot.bio: The Ming-style birthplace of travel writer Xu Xiake, with the study where he wrote his Travel Diaries.

spot.name: Huangshan Fort
spot.bio: A late Qing fort in the Jiangyin Fortress system, with gun emplacements, underground bunkers and observation posts.

spot.name: Mount Mao
spot.bio: Taoist holy mountain and birthplace of the Shangqing school, with about an hour's climb to the summit.

spot.name: Tianmu Lake
spot.bio: Lake south of Liyang with boat trips, a provincial tourist resort since 1993.

spot.name: Nanshan Bamboo Sea
spot.bio: Liyang's bamboo sea of about 2,300 hectares, with lakes, a historic area and a ground cable car.

spot.name: Xiang Yu's Ancestral Home
spot.bio: Hometown of Xiang Yu, with a temple, a statue and an ancient battlefield on Huanghe South Road.

spot.name: Santaishan Forest Park
spot.bio: National forest park on the shore of Luoma Lake in Hubin New District, in Suyu District.

spot.name: Suqian Museum
spot.bio: City museum on Suqian's history, customs, economic development and folk art.

spot.name: Sihong Ancient Xucheng Scenic Area
spot.bio: Scenic area on the heritage of the ancient Xu Kingdom, in the Southern New City of Sihong County.

spot.name: Yucheng Postal Stop
spot.bio: China's largest and best-preserved ancient courier station, built in the early Ming dynasty outside Gaoyou's South Gate.

spot.name: Zhenguo Temple
spot.bio: A Buddhist temple on a small Grand Canal island, known for a pagoda little changed since the Tang dynasty.

spot.name: Dafeng Milu Nature Reserve
spot.bio: National reserve on the Yellow Sea coast where Père David's deer were reintroduced in 1986.

spot.name: Yancheng China Sea Salt Museum
spot.bio: Museum on Yancheng's salt-making history, free to enter, in the building that also holds Yancheng Museum.
